overview.summary: Field research case study from immersive observation at a low-engagement KCPS high school, documenting real challenges and informing product design.
overview.context: Spent months as a co-teacher observing English classrooms across different grade levels, taking detailed notes on engagement, mental health, social environments, teaching methods, and problems.
overview.keyQuote: Progress emerges when we tend to the shadows, not just celebrate the light.
overview.privacyNote: All student and staff names in this case study are pseudonyms. Observations are de-identified field notes, not education records.

narratives.title: A Chance to Thrive
narratives.summary: Highlights state of engagement through storytelling - a lone scholar trying to focus while classroom chaos surrounds them.
narrative: The classroom, at first glance, resembled a deserted space more than a learning environment — except for a lone scholar in a red sports jersey at the center of the room. Upon further inspection, the students could be found sprawled on the floor, lost in video calls, conversations, and the endless scroll of social media, oblivious to the overwhelmed teacher at the front. Yet the young scholar, armed with quiet determination to push forward, strained to focus on the lecture.

Despite their efforts, the teacher continued lecturing — each word drifting into a void of indifference, unheard and unanswered. In a desperate attempt to regain control, a student was sent from the room — a brief disruption before attention returned to screens and side conversations.
The sense of disconnect lingered in the air, heavy and unresolved.

As the bell rang, the teacher, visibly defeated, offered an apology to the student in red. The student met their gaze, offering a small shrug. “It’s tough for everyone right now. I get it. There’s always tomorrow.” — before limping out the door, their injured leg a visible reminder of their struggles both seen and unseen.
The teacher managed a faint smile, but their eyes lingered on the emptying classroom. How many dreams were being quietly set aside, how much potential left unrealized, in moments like these?

alternateScene.title: Difficulty Enacting Punishment
alternateScene.note: A second true scene recorded in the same source document, showing the other side of the same failure - a teacher who cannot enforce a boundary.
narrative: Winter break had just ended and a teacher returned to class hoping for improved engagement and behavior — a fresh start, having announced expectations before the extended break. The students immediately returned to their default behavior.

The teacher had had enough. Steam bursting from his ears, face as red as a tomato, he decided it was time to make an example. He had addressed the class as a whole multiple times: “I’ve had enough of your talking, rudeness — I’m trying to give a lesson and this has to stop,” followed by “I’m going to call security for real. I don’t want to, but I will do it!”

Picking out two students at the front of the class who kept talking, the teacher said “Leave the class.” The student refused, and instead moved to a different spot in the room. Stressed and anxious, armed with a desire to keep their job and improve the situation, the teacher’s voice trembled and their hands shook: “That’s it! I’m calling security!”

The teacher made their way to the phone and called security to request a student be removed. The students darted out before security could even arrive. The rest — still spread around the room on the floor, laying down, on their phones — commented: “Wow. Teacher actually did it.”

The teacher then commented about how they hadn’t wanted to do it but felt forced. Later in the class they began to feel guilty for pulling the trigger, and apologized directly to the student’s friend, and subtly to the class as a whole.

narratives.callToAction: Depicts the dire need for solutions and information

narratives.title: Kidnapped From Education
narratives.statusNote: Author's own assessment: writing quality is mediocre and the sequence is confusing. Clarify before external use.
narratives.summary: Documents security failures and classroom disruptions - students being physically dragged from classrooms while security officers laugh.
narrative: There was a palpable tension in the third-floor hallway. Inside a classroom, a teacher began his lesson, a plea for twenty minutes of focused attention hanging in the air. The jammed printer denied him the paper copies the students preferred — a small but telling loss in a day of many. He needed to get through his presentation, not wanting to take up too much of “their time.”

The classroom door became a revolving portal. Students drifted in and out, some heading to the coat closet to grab their personal scents and spray them, oblivious to their disruption. Then came the dragging. Multiple students picked up a young girl by her hands and legs and dragged her out into the hallway. A security officer, present and observed by the students, laughed along with the others, underscoring their disregard for his presence. This wasn’t an isolated incident. The same officer had previously been seen playfully fighting with a student, blurring the lines between protector and participant.

Later, the teacher — armed with two students appearing as if they were his personal bodyguards — left the room to retrieve something. Meanwhile, I reflected on the fact that one of the students had mentioned she wished security would take their roles more seriously.

The teacher returned. A while later, the dragging happened again. And another student, hyped up by the activity, was seen crawling out of the classroom into the hallway, then returning with a scraped knee — a reminder of the damage done to their education.

At the end of class, the teacher, his face showing a clear recognition of my displeasure, acknowledged the day’s turmoil with a simple, “That was a bit much.” Later, in a conversation with the dean of culture — a man whom I wonder, is he blind to the chaos or fully aware of it? — I overheard the teacher offering a standard cover, pretending everything was fine, before I headed back downstairs to my room. It feels to me as if there is an unseen fear, a constant undercurrent of unease, which permeates the school but pools more heavily in certain areas. The students, deserving of a safe and nurturing learning environment, were instead subjected to a performance of chaos.

narratives.title: The Light at The End Of The Tunnel
narratives.summary: A fight intervention scene depicting security response, environmental decay, and the path to transformation through patience and consistent encouragement.
narrative: I stood in front of my locked classroom door in the science hallway, waiting for security to let me in. As I waited I began to hear muffled sounds of anger and pent-up frustration drifting from the corner, voices creeping around it. As the figures came darting into view, I began to understand what was happening and gained a clearer perspective on the events unfolding in front of me.

A single student, overflowing with energy, chased a group through the middle of the hall, her screams echoing the force of her movement. Their fight and disruptive behavior drew the attention of every neighboring classroom.

The student, having a lengthy track record of engagements, encouraged quick activity. One, two, three — security moved in. The lead guard grabbed the aggressor and pinned her against the wall, about a fifth of the way down the hall. He readied his pepper spray, his hand wavering over the button, a surge of adrenaline accompanying the unwanted anticipation of its use. The other officers and teachers converged on the scene, managing the gathering crowd and directing them back to their designated areas.

The student remained pinned to the wall and looked to her left, the direction she’d come from. The wall was bare, marred by cracked paint and bite-sized holes — a testament to past struggles. To her right, the lockers: some bolted shut, others mangled beyond repair. That’s when she saw me. I raised the paper attendance sheets in my hands to cover my eyes from the pepper spray, just in case.

With time and patience, the lead guard’s consistent encouragement began to take hold. A flicker of understanding, and a hint of change appeared in her eyes. Her rush of excitement faded, her posture softened, and her breathing steadied. She was gently guided to a calmer space — one that offered a chance to regroup and begin again.

My door clicked open, and I stepped inside for my planning period, ready to devise plans for growing and healing the next generation. As I sat down, the weight of the morning’s events pressed on me. I knew that real change would require more than discipline — it would take positive reinforcement, leadership, and a system to help students redirect their energy and heal their pain.

I looked at the attendance sheets in my hands. Each name was a story, and each day was a chance to guide a student toward a brighter future. But these stories are not unique to one classroom; they are part of a much larger narrative that calls for systemic change and innovative solutions across our society and the world.
narratives.keyMoment: A flicker of understanding, and a hint of change appeared in her eyes. Her rush of excitement faded, her posture softened, and her breathing steadied.

stateOfEducation.headline: The State of Education
stateOfEducation.subtitle: This isn't one school's failure. It's the system's.
statements: Teachers are alone in rooms built for compliance, not learning.
Kids fall through cracks the schedule was never designed to close.
Security responds to fights the environment provoked in the first place.
"Individualized attention" means one adult and thirty kids competing for it.
Every budget conversation is about buildings. None of them are about people.
The kids who need the most support get the least consistent adults.
stateOfEducation.closingStatement: We didn't build Expanse because a classroom was broken. We built it because the system around that classroom never gave anyone a chance to fix it.
